notes: Settlement 2026-11-07: base.deductions additional 500 exemption (what, 20 comparison lines): A said what other, B said what age_65_exemption, otherwise the same figures; PDF page 25 Line 5 says 'An additional $500 exemption is available ... if you are age 65 or older': an age-65 amount, so age_65_exemption (B). Threshold 40,000 for every status but married filing separately (20,000), at_or_over because the booklet says 'less than'.

Settlement 2026-11-07: base.deductions first-year child exemption (3 lines): A folded 3,000 into the 1,500 entry's condition, B wrote its own entry; PDF page 26 prints 'an amount of $3,000 instead of $1,500 for one tax year': its own entry (B).

Settlement 2026-11-07: base.deductions renter's, homeowner's and private school deductions (15 lines): A held them in notes, B as entries; PDF pages 16-18 and Schedule 2 lines 1, 2 and 8 print the amounts: kept as entries (B), with the Lake County credit bar added to the homeowner's condition from PDF page 16.

Settlement 2026-11-07: reliefs Social Security and railroad (9 lines): A wrote one entry, B two; PDF page 17 prints one rule under one heading for lines 5 and 6 with the same terms for both: one entry (A).
Settlement 2026-11-07: reliefs U.S. government interest who.basis (6 lines): A said return, B said each_person; PDF page 17 Line 4 tests neither spouse's age or status: return (A).

Settlement 2026-11-07: reliefs civil service annuity best_of_group: A said civil_service_annuity, B none; PDF page 19 says the two are combined up to 16,000 ('the combined deduction cannot exceed $16,000'), not that the filer chooses one, and each spouse of a couple may qualify: no best_of_group (B), the combined limit stays in cap_rule.

Settlement 2026-11-07: paying_states ['federal'] added to both civil service annuity entries, which neither reader did: PDF page 19 says 'federal civil service annuity income', so the entries do not reach Indiana state or local pensions, which public_pension would otherwise suggest.
Settlement 2026-11-07: disability retirement cite: A said PDF page 21, B said PDF page 20; the deduction is printed on PDF page 20.

Settlement 2026-11-07: Department web page conflict: deductions.page.txt, marked 'Updated for 2023', describes a Military Service Deduction with a retiree test ('You were at least 60 years of age by the end of the year') and gives tier 1 Railroad Retirement income only in the civil service limit. The 2025 booklet has separate military deductions with no age test (PDF pages 18 and 22) and says tier 1 and tier 2 (PDF pages 19-20). The 2025 booklet governs; the web text is not used.

Rate: the 3% is printed on Form IT-40 line 8 ('multiply line 7 by 3% (.03)'), and again in the booklet's Group A Worksheet line B (PDF page 37) and its examples (PDF page 38). One rate for every filing status; no separate married-separate or head-of-household schedule is printed. The worksheet and examples are for the credit for taxes paid to other states.
The booklet prints no standard deduction. Indiana starts from federal AGI (IT-40 line 1), adds Schedule 1 add-backs, subtracts Schedule 2 deductions and Schedule 3 exemptions.

Government pension from another state, including a New York State pension: not found in the booklet. No line, deduction code or exclusion names it. The only retirement deductions printed are Social Security, railroad retirement, federal civil service annuity, military retirement and disability retirement, and PDF page 17 says 'Do not enter any other types of pension or retirement income on these lines.' PDF page 37 says 'If you received income from another state while you were an Indiana resident, you must report that income on your Indiana income tax return.' The reciprocal agreement (Group B: Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin; PDF page 38) 'only applies to income from wages, salaries, tips and commissions'; New York is in Group A, no agreement (PDF page 37).

Indiana's own state and local government pensions (including teachers): not found in the booklet; no deduction or exclusion. No sentence says they are taxed; they are in federal AGI, the starting point, and no line takes them out.

Private pensions, IRA distributions, employer-plan distributions and Roth conversions: not found in the booklet; no deduction or exclusion, and the words IRA (other than a historic modification code on PDF page 49), 401(k) and Roth do not appear as a rule. No sentence says they are taxed; they are in federal AGI, the starting point, and no line takes them out.

Military Service Deduction: PDF page 18 says the full amount of military pay from 2024, while PDF page 22 still calls it a deduction with a dollar limit ('Unlike the Military Service Deduction on line 7, this deduction does not have a dollar limit'). No limit is printed, so no cap is recorded.

Military Service and National Guard/reserve deductions use covers wages, and the disability retirement deduction uses covers other_income, because the schema has no kind for military pay and the booklet does not name the source of disability retirement income.

Adopted-child additional exemption (Schedule 3 line 6, Schedule IN-DEP-A, PDF pages 25-27): the dollar amount is not found in the sources; not recorded. Schedule 3 itself is not among the sources; the exemption amounts come from its line instructions.

Out of scope and not recorded as a relief (design.md, credits): Unified Tax Credit for the Elderly (Schedule 5 line 5, PDF page 30), a refundable low-income credit: age 65 or older by Dec. 31, 2025, IT-40 line 1 less than 10,000, six months' residence. Table A (joint filers both 65 or older): 140 under 1,000; 90 from 1,000 to 2,999; 80 from 3,000 to 9,999. Table B (one person 65 or older): 100, 50, 40 for the same bands.
Credit for taxes paid to other states (Schedule 6 line 5, PDF pages 37-38): the lesser of the tax paid to the other state, 3% of that income, or the tax on IT-40 line 8; not recorded as a relief.

Not recorded as reliefs (not retirement or investment income relief): state tax refund, unemployment compensation worksheet (PDF page 19), Indiana NOL, railroad unemployment and sickness benefits (code 624, PDF pages 22-23), Indiana lottery annuity (code 629), Indiana partnership long-term care premiums (code 608), health care sharing ministry (code 643), enterprise zone (code 603) and the other Line 11 codes on PDF pages 19-24.
Conformity: Line 1 assumes the Internal Revenue Code as in effect on Jan. 1, 2023; Indiana currently does not follow P.L. 119-21, and the 2026 General Assembly may change that (PDF page 3).
Indiana county income taxes (Schedule CT-40, IT-40 line 9) are local and out of scope; noted only. The county rate chart is on the back of Schedule CT-40, which is not in the sources.
Capital gains: not found in the booklet any rate or deduction that differs from ordinary income; list left empty. No surtax or recapture rule found.
Indexing: the booklet says nothing about inflation adjustment of any figure.

Format v1 adoption 2026-11-07: civil service annuity Social Security reduction: the gross amount received, not the federally taxable part. PDF page 19 says 'Less all amounts of Social Security income ... received by the civil service annuitant', and the PDF page 19-20 examples subtract the Social Security received. The order (taken off the lesser of the annuity and 16,000) was already in cap_rule.

reliefs.cap_rule: For each civil service annuitant: the lesser of the taxable civil service annuity included in federal AGI or 16,000, less all Social Security income and tier 1 and tier 2 Railroad Retirement income received by that annuitant (the income is taken from the lesser amount, not from the 16,000 first: annuity 6,000, Social Security 1,200 gives 4,800). The Social Security taken off is the full amount received (gross benefits), not the part taxable in federal AGI: the booklet says 'all amounts of Social Security income ... received', and its examples subtract the Social Security received (1,200; 6,300; 17,500). The deduction is not below 0 (Matthew: Social Security 17,500 over his annuity 13,700, no deduction). An annuity received both for oneself and as a surviving spouse: the combined deduction cannot exceed 16,000.

muni_interest.note: Interest from a direct obligation of a state or political subdivision other than Indiana is taxable by Indiana if acquired after Dec. 31, 2011 (Schedule 1 line 3 add-back); interest from obligations held or acquired before Jan. 1, 2012 is not subject to Indiana income tax. Obligations of Puerto Rico, Guam, Virgin Islands, American Samoa or Northern Mariana: no add-back. Indiana's own obligations: the add-back reaches only obligations other than Indiana's, and the Indiana-only Tax-exempt Bonds Deduction (code 636, PDF page 21) deducts interest from certain Indiana bonds that is included in federal gross income. The booklet does not say in one sentence that all Indiana obligations are exempt.
